explanation.headline: Call was the top play, and you found it.

paragraphs: You held J♠ Q♥ on the button, against Villain, a Sticky player, in the big blind. Pre-flop, you opened to 2.5 bb and Villain called.
The flop came 7♠ A♥ 9♣: Villain checked, you bet 1.5 bb and Villain raised to 4.5 bb. You faced 3 bb more to call, with 11 bb in the pot.
sections.title: The hand

paragraphs: You chose Call (EV 2.25 bb), the top play against Villain's range. Verdict: Best.
Your equity against Villain's whole range is 37.5%. Calling 3 bb into a pot of 11 bb needs 3 bb / (11 bb + 3 bb) = 21.4% equity; 37.5% is above that, so calling beats folding.
Right now you are ahead of 42.0% of Villain's range. The largest parts of the range are Strong value (42.6% of it; your equity 10%) and Air (24.6% of it; your equity 78%).
sections.title: The verdict

paragraphs: Villain is a Sticky player. Competent, but defends wide and calls down lighter than most.
Villain's range narrowed with each action: Pre-flop: calls; Flop: checks, then raises to 4.5 bb.
The range in the Range tab is the range this puzzle was graded on.
